chunks.text: Today we will talk about Paraguay.
Paraguay is a small, landlocked, and friendly country in South America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Paraguay?
Paraguay is in the center of South America.
It is next to Brazil, Argentina, and Bolivia.
It does not touch the sea.
It is a landlocked country, but it has many rivers, like the Paraguay River and Paraná River.
What is the capital city of Paraguay?
The capital city is Asuncion.
It is next to the Paraguay River.
Asuncion has parks, markets, museums, and colonial buildings.
It is the largest city in the country.
How many people live in Paraguay?
About 7.5 million people live in Paraguay.
Many people live in small towns and villages.
The country is mostly rural and many people work in farming.
What language do people speak in Paraguay?
Paraguay has two official languages, Spanish, Guarani, an indigenous language spoken by most people.
Many people are bilingual and mix both languages in daily life.
What is the weather like in Paraguay?
Paraguay has a warm and wet climate.
Hot summers from November to March, mild winters from June to August.
There is rain during most months.
The east is more humid and the west is more dry.
What does Paraguay look like?
Paraguay has forests and wetlands, planes and rivers.
The Grand Chaco, a dry flat area in the west, hills and greenland in the east.
It is a country of nature and peaceful landscapes.
What animals live in Paraguay?
You can find capybaras, monkeys and jaguars, birds like toucans and parrots, frogs, snakes and fish, cows, horses and chickens on farms.
What do people eat in Paraguay?
Food is simple, hearty and made with corn, cheese and meat.
Popular dishes, chippa, cheesy bread made with cassava flour.
Sopa Paraguaya, a thick cornbread, not a soup.
Bay fried pancake made of cheese and flour.
Asado grilled meat.
Locro corn stew with meat.
People also eat tropical fruits like mangoes and papayas.
What do people drink in Paraguay?
People love tarare, cold herbal tea, shared in groups, mate, a hot version of the same drink, fruit juice, coffee, water and sometimes beer.
Drinking tarare is a daily social tradition.
What is life like in Paraguay?
Life is simple, slow and community -based.
People enjoy spending time with family, working outdoors, sharing food and drink, playing guitar and singing, watching football.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, May 14 to 15 Holy Week, Samana Santa, San Juan Festival with games, food and fire jumping.
Christmas and New Year Tarare Day, a celebration of the national drink.
Some fun facts about Paraguay.
Paraguay is one of the few bilingual countries in the Americas.
The Paraguay River divides the country into two parts.
The flag has three horizontal stripes, red, white and blue.
Paraguay has a taipu dam, one of the largest hydroelectric dams in the world.
People often play harp music.
Now you know many things about Paraguay.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
I'm Emilie.
See you next time.
Goodbye.
